messages.en: in New York
After a difficult journey, we finally made it to New York
and successfully finished our performance!
You must've had a hard time riding the bus for 9 hours.
It was quite an experience.

messages.ko: 난 자느라 몰랐지만 자유의 여신상도 지나왔고
messages.en: I was asleep, so I didn't notice, but we passed the Statue of Liberty, too.
Niagara Falls?
We passed that, too.
And I even crossed a border on my own two feet. It was really...
a new experience.

messages.ko: 살면서 언제 미국을 비행기 안타고 가보겠어
messages.en: When else in my life would I ever get to travel to the US without taking a plane?
Hehe.
Apparently, that takeoff ban had only happened three times in the US.
We're part of that history...
We've had so many things happen to us,
and it's funny how we've been so unfairly treated by forces of nature.
It's fascinating.
The fire alarm going off at the hotel,
the fire alarm going off at the venue today,
and not being able to board the plane
were all caused by forces of nature, right?
Or were they forces of machinery...?
We even had a power outage in Taiwan.
Right?
Maybe we're going to become really successful.
I hope we've gotten all the hardships out of the way and that only good things are left for us.
So we had steak yesterday.
After hardship comes happiness.
It was really delicious.
Is New York steak on another level?
ㅋㄹㅋㄹㅋㄹㅋㄹㅋㄹㅋㄹ It's on a whole other level.
That's right. Chaewon tried to assassinate me.
That's so ridiculous.
There was an announcement saying they were investigating the cause of the fire alarm on the 6th floor.
I heard that announcement saying they were looking into it.
I woke up from sleeping
and asked, 'Hey, what did they say?'
And then,
they told me, 'They said to go to the 6th floor.'
That's what I was told.
So I sent a message in the group chat,
'They're telling us to go to the 6th floor..?'
And when I said that,
everyone freaked out
and started telling me not to go to the 6th floor.
They kept sending me messages ㅋㅅㅋㅅㅋㄹㅋㄹㅋ

messages.en: I'd have been someone who willingly walked right into it and got roasted like a whole chicken.
But during the last tour, too,
there was supposedly a robber at the hotel or something.
I heard about it,
and the police came and took them away.
ㅋㄹㅋㄹㅋㄹㅋㄹㅋㄹㅋ

messages.ko: 어머 그렇게 심각한 얘기를 태연하게 말하네 ㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋ
messages.en: Oh my, you're talking so casually about something that serious ㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋ
Anyway,
it was all just malfunctions,
and the person was caught and taken away, so it's all good ㅋㅅㅋㅅㅋㅅㅋㅋ
But seriously, when some time has passed and I look back on it,
I think this tour is going to be really memorable.
Do you have no sense of danger?..
I really do.
Back when I lived at my family home,
I heard there was a fire near the shops,
so I ran right over there
to check out what was happening.
I had this feeling that I could put the fire out myself.
That's the kind of thought I had.
I'm an extreme N, so
whenever I see a fire hose cabinet,

messages.ko: 내가 어떻게 움직여서 제일 효율적인 동선으로 저걸 꺼내서 불을 끌수있을까
messages.en: I start thinking about how I could move around and get it out in the most efficient way possible to put out the fire.

messages.ko: 부터 불도 끄고 사람도 구한 착한시민상 받는것까지
messages.en: My imagination goes all the way from putting out the fire to rescuing people and receiving a Good Citizen Award.
When I was in elementary school,
firefighters came to give us a safety lesson,
and they let us try putting out a fire ourselves.
I went out and tried it.
You know they only let a few people try that, right?
So you had a bit of a hero complex?
That's right.
But now that I'm in New York,
why haven't I become Spider-Man?
I always think about this:

messages.ko: 어느날 갑자기 숨겨진 내 능력을 알아서
messages.en: what if I suddenly discover a hidden ability one day
and find out I can crawl up walls?

messages.ko: 거미줄대신 막 당면 이런 거 나올듯
messages.en: Instead of spiderwebs, you'd probably shoot out glass noodles or something.
Then I'd open a malatang restaurant right away.
I'd recruit people who could produce each ingredient
and start a business,
a malatang restaurant where your food comes out in 0.2 seconds.
Something like that.
